newsitem.title: USA: US Senate cuts off filibuster on FedEx bill.
newsitem.headline: US Senate cuts off filibuster on FedEx bill.

text.p: The Senate voted Thursday to cut off a filibuster mounted by pro-labor senators in an effort to kill legislation they said would hamper efforts by Federal Express Corp truck drivers to join a union.
Sen. Edward Kennedy had blocked Senate adjournment by filibustering airports legislation that contains the FedEx provision.
Kennedy's opponents mustered more than the 60 votes required to limit debate.

Kennedy had sought to delete from the bill a provision ensuring that FedEx is covered by the Railway Labor Act, a law that would require the firm's truck drivers to organize nationally in order to join a union.
The National Labour Relations Act allows more easily attainable local bargaining units.
The Railway Labor Act covers airline pilots, and FedEx pilots are unionized. Its truck drivers are not.
Supporters of the FedEx provision in the airports bill said it merely corrected a drafting error made when Congress enacted earlier legislation. Kennedy called the provision "union-busting."
Although the Senate voted to end the filibuster, Kennedy was still technically allowed up to 30 hours of debate on the bill. But relatively swift passage of the bill appeared likely.
